verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。用丝弦的乐器。）　神啊，求你听我的呼求，侧耳听我的祷告！
verses.en: For the music director, to be played on a stringed instrument; written by David.O God, hear my cry for help.Pay attention to my prayer.

verses.zh: 我心里发昏的时候，我要从地极求告你。求你领我到那比我更高的磐石！
verses.en: From the remotest place on earth[NOTE:1] I call out to you in my despair.[NOTE:2] Lead me[NOTE:3] up to a rocky summit where I can be safe.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 61. The psalmist cries out for help and expresses his confidence that God will protect him.

Heb “from the end of the earth.” This may indicate (1) the psalmist is exiled in a distant land, or (2) it may be hyperbolic (the psalmist feels alienated from God’s presence, as if he were in a distant land).
The imperfect verbal form here expresses the psalmist’s wish or prayer.

verses.zh: 因为你作过我的避难所，作过我的坚固台，脱离仇敌。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] you are[NOTE:2] my shelter,a strong tower that protects me from the enemy.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “on to a rocky summit [that] is higher than I.”

verses.zh: 我要永远住在你的帐幕里！我要投靠在你翅膀下的隐密处！（细拉）
verses.en: I will be a permanent guest in your home;[NOTE:1] I will find shelter in the protection of your wings.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Heb “a strong tower from the face of an enemy.”

Heb “I will live as a resident foreigner in your tent permanently.” The cohortative is understood here as indicating resolve. Another option is to take it as expressing a request, “please let me live” (cf. NASB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 神啊，你原是听了我所许的愿；你将产业赐给敬畏你名的人。
verses.en: For you, O God, hear my vows;you grant me the reward that belongs to your loyal followers.[NOTE:1]
notes: I will find shelter in the protection of your wings. The metaphor compares God to a protective mother bird.

verses.zh: 你要加添王的寿数；他的年岁必存到世世。
verses.en: Give the king long life.Make his lifetime span several generations.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you grant the inheritance of those who fear your name.” “Inheritance” is normally used of land which is granted as an inheritance; here it refers metaphorically to the blessings granted God’s loyal followers. To “fear” God’s name means to have a healthy respect for his revealed reputation which in turn motivates one to obey God’s commands (see Ps 86:11).

verses.zh: 他必永远坐在　神面前；愿你预备慈爱和诚实保佑他！
verses.en: May he reign[NOTE:1] forever before God.Decree that your loyal love and faithfulness should protect him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “days upon days of the king add, his years like generation and generation.”sn It is not certain if the (royal) psalmist is referring to himself in the third person in this verse, or if an exile is praying on behalf of the king.
Heb “sit [enthroned].” The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive here, expressing the psalmist’s prayer.

verses.zh: 这样，我要歌颂你的名，直到永远，好天天还我所许的愿。
verses.en: Then I will sing praises to your name continually,[NOTE:1] as I fulfill[NOTE:2] my vows day after day.
notes: Heb “loyal love and faithfulness appoint, let them protect him.”
